summary.en: Move a dividing line across ten fruit cards, count its mistakes, and keep a better rule.
summary.bn: দশটি ফলের কার্ডে ভাগের রেখা সরাও, ভুল গুনে ভালো নিয়ম বেছে নাও।

notes: Conceptual paper activities need no programming; teacher reference programs run on Python 3.10 or newer.

sections.title: Be the learner and the judge
A reason to move the fence

practice.title: Move from three to four
practice.statementHtml: Count the changed mistakes when the ten-fruit fence moves from 3 to 4.
practice.answerHtml: At three, p4 and p5 are incorrectly called mango. At four, p4 joins the apple side and becomes correct; p5 stays wrong. The count drops from two to one.

practice.title: Try six
practice.statementHtml: Explain why the fence at 6 makes two errors on the ten cards.
practice.answerHtml: p6 and p10 are mangoes of size six. They lie on the apple side at this threshold. The five apples and the other three mangoes are correctly named, leaving two errors.

practice.title: Tied fences
practice.statementHtml: The search finds no errors at 5 and 5.5. Explain the tie convention and its limits.
hints: A convention chooses without discovering a universal truth.
practice.answerHtml: This lab keeps the smaller value, five. Either tied value fits these cards. The choice does not establish which would work better on unknown sizes between them; fresh evidence is needed.

practice.title: A contradiction
practice.statementHtml: Create two same-size cards that force at least one mistake in any size-only fence.
hints: Give the two cards different labels.
practice.answerHtml: Use size four, sweetness three, apple, and size four, sweetness eight, mango. Any size-only threshold gives both the same prediction. At least one name disagrees. A rule using another feature might do better.

quiz.prompt: With the fence at size 3, which known apple cards are on the mango side?
options: p4 and p5
Only p1
p6 and p10
No cards
quiz.explanation: p4 is size four and p5 is size five. Both exceed three but their known names are apple, giving two disagreements.

caption.en: Predict Apple on or left of size 3; Mango on the right.
caption.bn: আকার 3 বা বাঁয়ে আপেল, ডানে আম অনুমান।

quiz.prompt: Read the four-fence mistake chart. Which tried dividing size has the lowest count?
quiz.explanation: The plotted counts are two at three, one at four, zero at five and two at six. Five is lowest among these four positions.

caption.en: Actual mistake counts for four trial fences.
caption.bn: চারটি ভাগের রেখায় গোনা আসল ভুল।

quiz.prompt: On the size-four fence picture, what happens to p5?
options: It is predicted apple because sweetness is five
Its label changes to match the prediction
It is predicted mango although its label is apple
It is not counted because it lies above the line
quiz.explanation: A vertical fence uses size. p5 has size five, which is right of four, so the prediction and known name disagree.

caption.en: Predict Apple on or left of size 4; Mango on the right.
caption.bn: আকার 4 বা বাঁয়ে আপেল, ডানে আম অনুমান।

quiz.prompt: Our rule predicts apple on or left of the fence. At a size-five fence, what is predicted for size five?
options: Mango
The card is automatically ignored
Its sweetness must be used as the deciding clue
Apple
quiz.explanation: The stated convention includes equality on the apple side. A rule needs an agreed treatment of points on its boundary.

quiz.prompt: What does the threshold lab change during its search?
options: The size dividing value
The supplied true names to remove mistakes
The fruit measurements to fit a preferred answer
The meaning of sweetness at each step
quiz.explanation: Training compares candidate fences against fixed observations and labels. Changing the answers would not be an honest comparison.

quiz.prompt: Five and five-and-a-half both make zero mistakes. Which does this lab keep?
options: Five-and-a-half, because it comes later
Five, using its smaller-value tie convention
Neither, because ties make all learning impossible
Whichever makes the fruit physically sweeter
quiz.explanation: The search visits small values first and replaces its best only for fewer mistakes. It therefore retains the earlier tied position.

quiz.prompt: Why does sweetness not affect this vertical-fence prediction?
options: Sweetness cannot ever help any fruit model
All sweetness values are identical
Only the horizontal size coordinate decides the side
A label removes the vertical axis
quiz.explanation: This model deliberately uses size alone. A different model could use both features, but that is a different rule family.

quiz.prompt: An apple and mango have identical size. Can one vertical fence name both correctly?
options: Yes, any fence at the shared size assigns two answers
Yes, the later card automatically moves right
No, because no model can ever use another feature
No, both must receive the same size-based prediction
quiz.explanation: Equal sizes lie on the same side. The failure is a limitation of this model, not a proof that every possible model fails.

quiz.prompt: Which change adds genuinely new evidence for the fruit rule?
options: A correctly labelled fruit unlike the earlier examples
A hundred exact copies of the first card
Deleting every old mistake from the answer column
Renumbering all cards in reverse order
quiz.explanation: A new relevant case can reveal missing patterns. Extra copies or identifiers do not provide that variety.

quiz.prompt: Why might more examples fail to improve the result?
options: Learning must become worse whenever a card is added
They may repeat narrow cases or contain wrong labels
A large pile guarantees perfect labels
New examples cannot ever expose model limits
quiz.explanation: More data helps when its content is relevant and reliable. Size alone does not guarantee useful evidence.

quiz.prompt: A size-six apple arrives after training. What does the size-five rule do?
options: Predict apple because it can see the hidden name
Change the actual fruit into mango
Predict mango and make a mistake
Prove that the ten old labels were all wrong
quiz.explanation: Six exceeds five, so the saved rule says mango. New evidence can contradict a rule that fit the old collection.

quiz.prompt: What does “best” mean in the lab’s half-centimetre search?
options: Best on every future fruit in the world
Best among all imaginable learning methods
The most complicated possible boundary
Fewest known-card mistakes among the tried fences
quiz.explanation: The comparison is limited to a specified grid and the supplied cards. Other rule families or later cases are outside that claim.

keyPoints.en: A threshold turns a measured size into a name prediction.
keyPoints.bn: Threshold মাপ থেকে নাম অনুমান করে।

keyPoints.en: Known labels let you count wrong guesses.
keyPoints.bn: জানা লেবেল দিয়ে ভুল গোনা যায়।

keyPoints.en: Training compares possible rules using those counts.
keyPoints.bn: ট্রেনিংয়ে সেই ভুল দেখে নিয়ম তুলনা হয়।

keyPoints.en: Tied rules need a stated choice convention.
keyPoints.bn: সমান হলে বাছার রীতি বলতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: The best rule here is best only among the tried fences.
keyPoints.bn: এখানের সেরা মানে চেষ্টা করা রেখাগুলোর মধ্যে সেরা।

keyPoints.en: New examples can expose missing clues or a weak model.
keyPoints.bn: নতুন উদাহরণ অনুপস্থিত ইঙ্গিত বা মডেলের সীমা ধরায়।

examQuestions.question: Using the ten-fruit cards, count mistakes at thresholds 3, 4, 5 and 6 under the stated apple-through-threshold convention.
examQuestions.answerHtml: At three, p4 and p5 disagree: two. At four, only p5 disagrees: one. At five, all names match: zero. At six, p6 and p10 disagree: two. The counts are 2, 1, 0, 2.

examQuestions.question: Explain why trying a new threshold and checking a new fruit are different operations.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Trying thresholds uses known labels to choose the rule. Checking a new fruit applies a rule already chosen, records a prediction and only then reveals the answer. The latter can provide evidence about transfer.

examQuestions.question: Describe an honest paper search over several dividing positions.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Keep measurements and labels fixed. State which side includes equality. For each position, predict every label and count disagreements. Apply a declared tie convention, then assess the saved rule on separately hidden cards.

examQuestions.question: Explain two reasons a zero training mistake count might not transfer to tomorrow.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Tomorrow may include different fruit types or ranges absent from the cards. The size-only rule may also miss useful sweetness or weight information. No old error count covers every new situation; use representative fresh checks.
